experiment.name: phase1_depth_operand
description: Does the zero-operand step scale with how far the operand travels?
This settles a contradiction between two results the chapter already
reports. Section 4's depth ladder says cost per byte rises ~68x from an
L1-resident working set to a DRAM-resident one. Section 8 says the all-zero
baseline is anomalously cheap, worth +349 mW, and that every delta quoted
against it carries that constant. Both were measured, but the step was
measured on ws_l3_x8 alone, and the two do not compose without knowing how
the step scales:
- If the step is a constant in WATTS, dividing it by throughputs spanning
41-741 GB/s corrects each depth by a different amount per byte. The
ladder collapses to ~5.5x, L3 and DRAM become indistinguishable, and
the L1 row goes negative -- i.e. L1-resident movement would leak
nothing beyond the zero anomaly.
- If the step is a constant in pJ/BYTE, section 4 stands as published.
- If the step scales with the effect at that depth, both readings are
wrong and the step is not a baseline offset at all but part of the
same depth-dependent transport term.
Nothing measured so far distinguishes these, and they give opposite
headlines. Note the third is already the most likely: the constant-watt
reading needs a +349 mW step inside an L1 row whose entire HW-0-to-HW-32
effect is +228 mW, and the constant-pJ/byte reading needs +1.75 W there.
Both are arithmetically impossible, which is itself informative -- but a
measured intercept per depth is what the chapter has to quote.
The same grid is the interaction term the combined leakage model needs.
Phase 1 so far delivers four characterisations -- depth, weight, distance,
instruction -- each with one factor varied and the others fixed, never
combined and never tested out of sample. Fitting dP = a(depth) + b(depth)*HW
here gives the first term of that model with its depth dependence measured
rather than assumed.
DESIGN. Four depths x four Hamming weights, each run contrasting the test
operand against an all-zero working set exactly as the weight sweep did, so
the L3 column is directly comparable to it. Weights 1 and 2 sit below the
discontinuity's shoulder and pin the low-end level; 8 and 32 pin the slope.
That is a 2+2 design: the step at each depth is the gap between the low
pair and the high pair extrapolated back to zero, and it needs no
assumption that the curve is linear through the low end -- the low-end
sweep already showed it is not.
Bit patterns are held identical across depths and reused from the earlier
sessions (0x00000008, 0x01000040, 0x0180D203, 0xFFFFFFFF), so a difference
between depths is a depth difference and not a placement difference, and
each L3 row has a published value to reproduce.
ws_l2_x8 carries no A/A of its own; three controls spanning L1 to DRAM are
enough to bound the noise floor across the range, and aa_l3 is the session
gate. L1 gets one because it is the row whose corrected effect could go
negative, and its whole effect is only +228 mW; DRAM gets one because it is
the poorly-conditioned victim in the set and has failed this gate before.
TWO-BUFFER A/A. Every ws_* contrast confounds condition with buffer
address: ws_init maps one buffer per slot and ws_get assigns a slot per
distinct selector, so conditions 0 and 1 read from different mappings.
A normal A/A cannot see that, because holding the same selector twice
yields one slot. But ws_get keys its cache on the full 64-bit selector
while ws_fill uses only the low 32 bits, so 0x00000000_5A5A5A5A and
0x00000001_5A5A5A5A allocate two distinct buffers with bit-identical
contents. Same data, different addresses, everything else equal. If that
reads non-zero, page colouring or slice mapping is contributing to every
A/B result in the project and the gate should fail loudly; it is declared
a control so that it does.
SHAM-B. The existing A/A controls all sit at the harness's quiet noise
floor (between-run SD 4.6-10 mW) while the claims they certify sit at ~2 W,
where the between-run SD is ~100 mW. sham_l3_hw16 contrasts an operand
against its own complement -- both HW 16, both homogeneous, so both weight
and distance are matched and the expected difference is zero -- on top of
the full ~1.2 W of common signal. Its between-run spread is the noise floor
for large effects, which is the number the chapter currently does not have.
It is deliberately NOT declared a control: a non-zero result here is the
bit-placement finding, not an instrument failure.
warmup_blocks is 8 throughout rather than 4, uniform across depths so the
comparison is not confounded by how much transient each row discarded.
ws_dram_x8 faults in 2 x 32 MB per thread under MAP_POPULATE and is the
reason the flag exists; 8 blocks is about a second of recording and costs
the session a minute in total.
Roughly 66 runs at ~80 s each: about 90 minutes. Dropping the hw02 row
costs the low-end redundancy and saves ~16 minutes if that is needed.

runs.label: aa_l1
runs.comment: Noise floor at L1, where the whole effect is only +0.23 W.

runs.label: l1_hw32
runs.comment: HW 32. Reproduces vol_x8 from the traffic-volume sweep (+0.228 W).

runs.label: l2_hw32
runs.comment: HW 32. Reproduces depth_l2 (+1.105 W).

runs.label: aa_l3
runs.comment: Session A/A gate, on the victim every other session used.

runs.label: l3_hw01
runs.comment: HW 1. Predict +0.42 W from the weight sweep, +0.41 W pooled.

runs.label: l3_hw02
runs.comment: HW 2. Predict +0.44 W from the low-end sweep.

runs.label: l3_hw08
runs.comment: HW 8. Predict +0.71 W from the weight sweep.

runs.label: l3_hw32
runs.comment: HW 32. Predict +1.90 W; also reproduces l3_forward (+1.841 W).

runs.label: aa_dram
runs.comment: DRAM is the poorly-conditioned victim and has failed this gate before (+15.4 mW, all three repeats positive).

runs.label: dram_hw32
runs.comment: HW 32. Reproduces depth_dram (+0.868 W).

runs.label: aa_l3_2buf
runs.comment: 0x00000000_5A5A5A5A vs 0x00000001_5A5A5A5A. ws_fill uses the low 32 bits, so both buffers hold 0x5A5A5A5A; ws_get keys on all 64, so they are different mappings. Same data, different addresses -- the address confound no ordinary A/A can see.

runs.label: sham_l3_hw16
runs.comment: 0x05A5E34F vs its complement 0xFA5A1CB0. Both HW 16, both homogeneous, so weight and distance are both matched and the expected difference is zero -- but it sits on ~1.2 W of common signal, so its between-run spread is the noise floor at effect scale. Not declared a control: a non-zero result is the placement finding, not an instrument failure.

runs.label: anchor_hw16
runs.comment: Cross-session anchor. 0x05A5E34F, HW 16, read +1.133, +1.215 and +1.228 W in the three earlier sessions. Kept out of the per-depth fits so all four depths share one 4-point design.
